title: Addition of completed tensor shifts on good representatives
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite coefficient extension E/Q_ell and a scheme W. Use the actual completed tensor T, its good flat-term K-flat representatives, and arbitrary families of left and right natural comparisons sigma^1_r and sigma^2_r satisfying the finite-tensor and Roos-cone normalization predicates [def-pur-integral-tensor-shift-properties, def-pur-integral-operation-complex-models]. For every two good complexes P,Q and a,b in Z, at (QP,QQ) each direct comparison sigma^k_(a+b) is the composite of the input shift-addition map, sigma^k_b evaluated with the indicated argument shifted by a, the b-shift of sigma^k_a, and the inverse output shift-addition map. These are component equalities only on good representatives. No zero law, comparison on arbitrary derived inputs, or coherent CommShift structure is asserted.

proof.text: Apply the assumed left and right representative normalization squares to a, b and a+b. Good complexes remain good after shift. At every finite level, total-tensor generator extensionality identifies the direct first-slot shift with its composite because both coefficients are 1. For the second slot the coefficients agree by ((a+b)*i).negOnePow = (a*i).negOnePow * (b*i).negOnePow. The tower comparisons already commute with all quotient transitions, so the equalities hold as tower maps.

proof.text: Project the product comparisons onto each factor to obtain their addition equation. On the two cone summands the coefficients are 1 and (a+b).negOnePow, respectively; the composite has 1 and a.negOnePow*b.negOnePow. Int.negOnePow_add identifies these. Cone extensionality proves equality, and the canonical shift associativity and commutation identities carry it through the final shift [-1]. This uses actual chain cones, not uniqueness of completions of triangles.

proof.text: Localize this chain equality. Substitute the three good-model normalization squares in each slot. Naturality and addition coherence of DerivedCategory.Q.commShiftIso combine the input and output quotient comparisons. Cancel the input isomorphisms and the shifted representative comparison, leaving exactly the two displayed component identities on the images of P and Q. There is no descent to arbitrary derived objects in this lemma.

lean.statement:
theorem completedTensorShift_add_on_good (W : Scheme.{u})
    (sl : ∀ r : ℤ, tensorShiftFirst (Integral l E W) r ⋙ integralCompletedTensor l E W ≅
      integralCompletedTensor l E W ⋙ shiftFunctor (Integral l E W) r)
    (sr : ∀ r : ℤ, completedTensorShiftSecond (Integral l E W) r ⋙
      integralCompletedTensor l E W ≅
        integralCompletedTensor l E W ⋙ shiftFunctor (Integral l E W) r)
    (hsl : ∀ r : ℤ, integralTensorLeftProperty l E W r (sl r))
    (hsr : ∀ r : ℤ, integralCompletedTensorRightShiftProperty l E W r (sr r))
    (a b : ℤ) (P Q : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E W).FullSubcategory) :
    let T := integralCompletedTensor l E W
    let M : Integral l E W := DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj
    let N : Integral l E W := DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q.obj
    ((sl (a + b)).hom.app (M, N) =
      T.map ((shiftFunctorAdd (Integral l E W) a b).hom.app M, 𝟙 N) ≫
        (sl b).hom.app (M⟦a⟧, N) ≫
        (shiftFunctor (Integral l E W) b).map ((sl a).hom.app (M, N)) ≫
        (shiftFunctorAdd (Integral l E W) a b).inv.app (T.obj (M, N))) ∧
    ((sr (a + b)).hom.app (M, N) =
      T.map (𝟙 M, (shiftFunctorAdd (Integral l E W) a b).hom.app N) ≫
        (sr b).hom.app (M, N⟦a⟧) ≫
        (shiftFunctor (Integral l E W) b).map ((sr a).hom.app (M, N)) ≫
        (shiftFunctorAdd (Integral l E W) a b).inv.app (T.obj (M, N)))
